title: How whisky came to India
sub: Two hundred years in forty seconds.

cards.head: 1820s
cards.sub: A British brewer, Edward Dyer, sets up in the hills.
cards.body: His brewery site later became India’s first distillery.

cards.head: 1982
cards.sub: Amrut starts making whisky from malted barley.
cards.body: Most Indian ‘whisky’ was made from molasses. This was different.

cards.head: 2004
cards.sub: India’s first single malt launches. In Scotland.
cards.body: Amrut debuted in Glasgow on 24 August 2004. Bold move.

cards.head: 2023
cards.sub: Indri wins ‘Best in Show’ at the Whiskies of the World Awards.
cards.body: A distillery from a Haryana town, on the world stage.

cards.head: 2025
cards.sub: Indian malt makers apply for a GI tag.
cards.body: Like Darjeeling tea, Indian single malt wants a protected name.

cards.head: India drinks more whisky than any other country.
cards.tip: Hum sirf peete nahi, banate bhi hain.

caption:
How did whisky come to India? 🇮🇳🥃 Two hundred years of Indian whisky history in 40 seconds.

1820s: Edward Dyer sets up a brewery in Kasauli. The site later becomes India’s first distillery.
1982: Amrut starts making whisky from malted barley in Bengaluru.
2004: India’s first single malt, Amrut, launches in Glasgow.
2023: Indri wins Best in Show at the Whiskies of the World Awards.
2025: Indian malt makers apply for a GI tag.
Today: India drinks more whisky than any other country.
